newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-RAIN SUSPENDS PLAY IN MILLION DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RAIN SUSPENDS PLAY IN MILLION DOLLAR.

text.p: Heavy overnight and morning rain suspended play after just one and a half hours of first-round action in the 1996 Million Dollar Challenge at the par-72 Gary Player Country Club on Thursday.
Play was eventually suspended at 1115 GMT, despite a prompt start, after 22 millimetres of rain fell on the course in the morning.
Chief rules official for the tournament, Dennis Bruyns, said some of the greens had become unplayable, while most of the saturated bunkers on the course were "unfair".
Bruyns said the Million Dollar Challenge had never in its 15-year history seen an uncompleted day's play.
The first round would resume at 0530 GMT on Friday, Bruyns said, with the second round beginning on time in the afternoon, weather permitting.
Germany's Bernhard Langer, the Million Dollar champion in 1985 and 1991, set the early pace with American Steve Stricker in the persistent drizzle on Thursday.
With the players able to take preferred lies on the fairways to clear mud from their balls, the pair moved to two-under for the tournament before they both dropped shots at the 400-metre fifth.
Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, with a birdie four at the 503-metre second, also moved to one-under for the tournament to share the early threeway tie for the lead when play was suspended.
Nick Price (Zimbabwe), Ian Woosnam (Wales), defending champion Corey Pavin (U.S.), Mark Brooks (U.S.), Ernie Els (South Africa) and Mark O'Meara (U.S.) were all level-par for their rounds.
Corey Pavin said the decision to start play on time in the morning was fully justified.
"The big question mark was with the bunkers and the tournament committee decided to go out and play -- and that was fine.

"Everybody had the same situation and everyone knew that you had to try and avoid the bunkers! If you hit it into casual water in the bunkers and had to drop, your ball could plug in the bunker," he said.

"I didn't take my own advice very well because I drove in the bunker at the first hole and had to do that. It's unfortunate that the tournament couldn't stay on schedule, but I think by the end of tomorrow we'll be right back on track."
